summary: This program asks whether you prefer Celsius, stores that answer as a True/False value, then reads a temperature and gives clothing advice. If you chose Fahrenheit, it converts your number to Celsius first so the comparisons still make sense.

lines.text: The comparison `== "yes"` produces a Boolean, so `use_celsius` holds True or False rather than the text the user typed. Calling `.strip()` removes stray spaces and `.lower()` folds "YES" or "Yes" down to "yes", so small differences in typing still count as agreement; anything else, including "no", makes it False.
A Boolean variable can be tested on its own — there is no need to write `if use_celsius == True`, because the variable already is the answer to the question.
`input` always hands back text, so `float` is needed to turn "70" into a number you can do arithmetic and comparisons with.

The Fahrenheit reading is converted into Celsius and stored in `temp`, so the rest of the program only ever deals with one scale. This is why 70°F is treated as mild instead of triggering the sunscreen advice.
`elif` is only reached when the `if` above it was False, and the final `else` catches everything left over — every temperature between 10 and 30 lands there.
